title: Table Operations (table library)
summary: The table library: insert, remove, find, sort, concat, move, create, clone, freeze — the standard toolkit for working with arrays and tables.

methods.name: table.insert
methods.description: Append value at the end, or insert at position pos (shifting later elements up).

methods.name: table.remove
methods.description: Remove and return the element at pos (default: last). Later elements shift down.

methods.name: table.find
methods.description: Luau addition. First index whose element == value, or nil.

methods.name: table.sort
methods.description: Sort the array part in place. Optional comparator(a, b) returns true if a comes first.

methods.name: table.concat
methods.description: Join array elements into one string — the fast way to build big strings.

methods.name: table.move
methods.signature: table.move(a1, f, e, t, a2?) --> table
methods.description: Copy elements a1[f..e] into positions starting at t (in a2, or a1 itself).

methods.name: table.create
methods.description: Luau addition. Pre-sized array, optionally filled with value.

methods.name: table.clone
methods.description: Luau addition. Shallow copy of a table.

methods.name: table.freeze
methods.description: Luau addition. Makes t read-only; writes error. Freezes recursively for typed tables.

methods.name: table.clear
methods.description: Luau addition. Empties a table in place, keeping its capacity.

explanation.whatItIs: Built-in functions for the everyday surgery of tables: adding, removing, sorting, joining, copying.
explanation.whyItExists: These operations are needed constantly; builtins are battle-tested and faster than hand-rolled loops.
whenToUse: `find` to locate a value in a small array
`sort` with a comparator for leaderboards: `table.sort(scores, function(a, b) return a.points > b.points end)`
`concat` whenever you build one string from many pieces
whenNotToUse: `table.find` on huge arrays every frame — use a dictionary set instead
`table.remove(t, 1)` in a hot loop on big arrays is O(n) each time; consider `table.clear` + rebuild or a proper queue
tips: `table.sort` comparator must be a strict ordering (return false for equal items) or you can get infinite loops/errors
`table.freeze` is perfect for constant config tables — typos then error loudly instead of silently nil-ing
`table.clone` is shallow: nested tables remain shared
commonMistakes: Calling `table.insert` on a dictionary and wondering where the value went (it appends to the array part)
Forgetting `table.sort` mutates the original table — clone first if you need the original order
Using `table.remove` without checking the table isn't empty

examples.title: Leaderboard sorting
examples.code:
local scores = {
    { name = "Alice", points = 90 },
    { name = "Bob", points = 120 },
    { name = "Cara", points = 75 },
}

table.sort(scores, function(a, b)
    return a.points > b.points   -- highest first
end)

for rank, entry in scores do
    print(rank, entry.name, entry.points)
end
--> 1 Bob 120 / 2 Alice 90 / 3 Cara 75
